evidence.quote: the South African avocado season extended from February to October, but with new plantings at higher elevations and more southerly latitudes harvesting now takes place from February in the to mid-January.
evidence.doc: SA Avocado Industry Overview – South African Avocado Growers' Association (SAAGA)

harvestMonths.notes: Source text has a garbled clause ('...takes place from February in the to mid-January') indicating the season is extending later into the year with new higher-elevation/southerly plantings; the core Feb-Oct figure is the clear, unambiguous statement so it is used as the general-SA range.

harvestMonths.region: South Africa - warm subtropical regions (Hass cultivar)

evidence.quote: Hass ... Flowering and harvesting months ... Warm regions ... Flowering: July - September ... Harvesting: June - October
evidence.doc: Directorate Communication: Cultivation of Avocados (South African Dept. of Agriculture / ARC-Institute for Tropical and Subtropical Crops)

harvestMonths.notes: Hass and Hass-type cultivars make up ~80% of SA nursery avocado trees per SAAGA. 'Warm regions' in this DAFF/ARC guide corresponds to lowveld areas such as Tzaneen/Levubu (Limpopo) and Mpumalanga lowveld.

harvestMonths.region: South Africa - cool subtropical regions (Hass cultivar)

evidence.quote: Hass ... Cool regions ... Flowering: August - October ... Harvesting: August - December
evidence.doc: Directorate Communication: Cultivation of Avocados (South African Dept. of Agriculture / ARC-Institute for Tropical and Subtropical Crops)

harvestMonths.notes: 'Cool regions' corresponds to higher-altitude/mistbelt areas such as the KZN midlands and cooler parts of Mpumalanga/Limpopo.

evidence.quote: Hass was the most precocious cultivar, with bearing starting in the second season, and reaching 10 t ha-1 by year three.
evidence.doc: Wolstenholme, Kaiser & Palmer, 'Yield Potential of Intensively Managed Avocados in the Natal Midlands — The Early Bearing Years', South African Avocado Growers' Association Yearbook 1991, 14:15-18

yearsToFirstCrop.notes: Bruyns Hill, Natal Midlands bioclimatic group 2; irrigated Hass on clonal Duke 7 rootstock, 7 x 7 m (200 trees/ha), planted 1982–1984. The paper reports Hass starting in its second season and Fuerte in its third. The two-to-three-year reference describes those trial cultivars, not every avocado or nursery starting age.

evidence.quote: Hass was the most precocious and consistent bearer, averaging over 15 t ha-1 and reaching an average of 20 t ha-1 by the sixth year. Thereafter, an average yield of about 22,5 t ha-1 appears to be sustainable.

yearsToFullBearing.notes: In this irrigated, intensively managed Natal Midlands trial, Hass reached about 20 t/ha at age 6 and orchards approached maximum sustainable average yield by age 8. This is a trial-specific bearing reference; there is no national plateau or automatically interpolated age-yield curve.

evidence.quote: reaching an average of 20 t ha-1 by the sixth year. Thereafter, an average yield of about 22,5 t ha-1 appears to be sustainable ... At a spacing of 7 x 7 m (200 trees per ha)

yieldKgPerTreeMature.notes: Same-trial arithmetic at the initial 200 trees/ha: 20,000 kg/ha / 200 = 100 kg/tree at age 6; sustainable average 22,500 kg/ha / 200 = 112.5 kg/tree. At age 3, 10,000 kg/ha / 200 = 50 kg/tree equivalent. These are average-equivalent reference values for the named Hass/Duke 7 orchard conditions, not measured individual-tree yields or default production for a different density, cultivar, climate or management. Intermediate ages are not inferred.

chillUnits.notes: No SA source found quantifying a chill-unit requirement for avocado. Avocado is evergreen/subtropical, but no source located explicitly states 'no chill requirement', so left null per instructions rather than assumed.

evidence.quote: Hass, an A-type flowerer, tended to be out of phase with Fuerte and Rinton on a seasonal yield basis ... favourable temperatures at fruit-set (especially in B flowering type cultivars such as Fuerte) can result in heavy cropping

pollination.notes: SA source confirms avocado's type A / type B protogynous dichogamous flowering system (temporal separation of male and female phases within a single tree) rather than stating self-fertility directly. Supporting SA quote on the practical effect: DAFF/ARC 'Cultivation of Avocados' guide lists for Fuerte (a Type B cultivar) 'Comments: fruit set increased by a pollinator' (http://www.avocadosource.com/international/south_africa_papers/cultivation_of_avocados.pdf, p.5), i.e. trees do set fruit alone (self-fertile) but cross-pollination with the opposite flower type improves fruit set — hence 'partly-self-fertile' rather than 'self-fertile' or 'needs-cross-pollinator'.

supplementaryReferences.title: Hass age benchmarks — irrigated Natal Midlands trial
supplementaryReferences.doc: Wolstenholme, Kaiser & Palmer (1991), SAAGA Yearbook 14:15–18; reflowed PDF
supplementaryReferences.note: Hass on Duke 7, initially 200 trees/ha at Bruyns Hill (Natal Midlands bioclimatic group 2), with intensive irrigation and nutrition. Age 3: 10,000 kg/ha; age 6: 20,000 kg/ha; sustainable average about 22,500 kg/ha. Same-study density permits equivalents of 50 kg/tree at age 3 and 100 kg/tree at age 6; there is no reference for every intermediate age. These orchard benchmarks are conditional on good resources, comparable climate and timely orchard management, including Phytophthora control and thinning; do not auto-fill farm quantities.

gaps: Could not find a SA primary/grower-body source stating a numeric chill-unit requirement for avocado; searched ARC-ITSC, DAFF/nda.agric.za (page returned HTTP 503), SAAGA yearbooks, and general 'chill unit' South Africa searches (mostly returned deciduous-fruit chill-model literature, none avocado-specific).

Years-to-first-crop and yield/tree figures are sourced from one detailed KZN Natal-midlands trial (SAAGA 1991) plus a corroborating SAAGA 1995 KZN paper; did not find an equivalent quantified trial for the Limpopo/Mpumalanga lowveld (the largest SA production area) despite searching ARC-ITSC and SAAGA yearbook archives — noted as a regional gap.
